# bugs #4070: sdas8051 assembles the address of the fourth byte of an __sfr32 as 0xFF

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4070/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Choose between this patch, which keeps the object format, and the upstream asxxxx design. sdas390 was not built or run.
- Patch: [bugs-4070.patch](../../patches/bugs-4070.patch), commit [`b2a58f154`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/b2a58f154e32bf6ae164eb022bf853d1d985bfbf). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For every `__sfr32`, sdas8051 assembles the address of the fourth byte as `0xFF`. The file
attached to the first comment assigns 0 to `__sfr32 __at(0xa4a5a6a7)`. It was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51` on r17192 with the earlier patches of this report, with a read of the SFR into a
global variable added. The listing has `F5 A7`, `F5 A6`, `F5 A5`, and `F5 FF` for the four
writes, `85 FF 0B` for the read of the fourth byte, and `FFA5A6A7` for the symbol.

## Cause

The compiler writes the operand of the fourth instruction as `((_X >> 24) & 0xFF)`. `minit` in
`sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` calls `exprmasks(3)`, which sets `a_bytes`, the number of address bytes in
the T lines, and the masks of `rngchk` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asexpr.c`. The assembler applies `rngchk`
to every constant and to the result of every binary operator, and with these masks it
sign-extends the value from bit 23. Every SFR address is `0x80` or higher, so bit 23 is set in
every list of four addresses, and `0xa4a5a6a7` is `0xffa5a6a7` when the shift is applied.
`rngchk` returned its argument until [r13068](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13068/), in
which the range check of asxxxx 5.40 was merged.

## Fix

`minit` calls `exprmasks(4)` and then sets `a_bytes` to 3. Expression values have 32 bits. The
object file keeps the header line `XH3` and 3 address bytes in its T lines. The S line of the
symbol has `DefA4A5A6A7`, and without the patch it has `DefFFA5A6A7`. sdld masks symbol values to
24 bits. The map file lists `00A5A6A7` with and without the patch, and sdld links an object file
from sdas8051 without the patch and one from sdas8051 with the patch without a message.

## Decision

The patch keeps the object format. The ticket has two other designs.

- The patch attached to the tenth comment adds `valmasks` to `asexpr.c`, and `minit` calls
  `exprmasks(3)` and `valmasks(4)`. By the code, `a_bytes` and the three masks then have the
  values that this patch gives them. That patch changes code that the assemblers share, and this
  one changes only `minit`. The patch in the ticket was not applied here.
- In the last comment a maintainer prefers the design of upstream asxxxx, which has one width
  and other relocation flags and output functions. With `exprmasks(4)` alone, sdas8051 writes 4
  address bytes to the T lines, and the seventh comment shows that sdld then relocates wrongly.
  This design was not tried.

With this patch, and by the code with the one in the ticket, hand-written assembly gets other
results for values that do not fit in 24 bits as signed numbers. Constants from 0x800000 to
0xffffff are positive, and constants above 0xffffff are not truncated.

| Source line | Without the patch | With the patch |
|---|---|---|
| `mov a,#(0x800000 >> 20)` | `74 F8` | `74 08` |
| `.iflt 0xC00000` | true | false |
| `.dw 0x12345678 >> 16` | `00 34` | `12 34` |
| `mov 0x1000080,a` | `F5 80` | "Page 0 Address Error" |

With `-v`, sdas8051 reports error `v` for `X32 = 0xa4a5a6a7` without the patch and does not
report a value with it. Negative values, labels, and values below 0x800000 give the bytes that
they give without the patch. By the source, sdas390 sets the expression width from the address
width in `sdas/as8xcxxx/ds8mch.c`. The patch does not change sdas390, which was not built or run.

sdasstm8, sdasf8, sdasrab, and the pdk assemblers call `exprmasks(3)`, and the patch does not
change them. Bug #3527 reports the 24-bit evaluation for a pdk assembler. Support request #210
reports it for sdas8051 with the constant 125000000 in inline assembly, and this patch fixes that
case.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4070.c` declares an `__sfr32` over the registers of timer 0 and
timer 2, a second one with the reverse address list, and the four registers as `__sfr` and
`__sfr16`. It writes through one declaration and reads through the others, as the ninth comment
proposes. With sdas8051 without the patch it fails 8 of its 16 assertions on mcs51-small,
mcs51-large, mcs51-small-stack-auto, and mcs51-large-stack-auto, the four variants that were
run. With the patch it passes on the six mcs51 variants. `sfr16.c` passes with the defect,
because it reads and writes its `__sfr32` only as a whole.

sdas8051 with and without the patch assembled the 29181 assembly files of the regression suite
for the six mcs51 variants, 1083 assembly files of the library, and the `.s` files of the mcs51
library for seven models. The `.rel`, `.lst`, and `.sym` files are identical except for the tests
`sfr16` and `bug-2235`, where the fourth address of the `__sfr32` and the value in its S line
differ. With this patch and the patch for bug #3973 added to the earlier patches of this report
on r17192, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80,
and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.
The code size of every other test is equal with and without the two patches.
